# About me

I have a background in policy and economics, and am now a PhD candidate in Economic Sociology, Organisation, and Labour (ESOL) at the University of Milan. My research examines how experiencing or witnessing economic hardship in one’s social and geographical proximity erodes trust in political institutions. My work draws on quantitative, qualitative, and computational tools.

I occasionally take on projects outside my main field of interest including, most recently, public health research.

On the rare occasions in which I'm off work, I am also involved in cultural and social organisations, such as *Ippogogo APS* and *RxR - una Regione per Restare*.

This site accomodates my research work, the occasional blog post, and some teaching material.
